verdicts.reason: The candidate is a regression test for the reported behavior: validators.mac_address must not accept the mixed-separator form 'aa:bb-cc-dd:ee:ff', while uniform ':' and '-' forms remain valid. The expectation source (input/issue.md) states the mixed form should yield a validators.ValidationError rather than True, and uniform forms should still be accepted. Execution was real: target_calls shows validators.mac_address called 5 times and target_origins binds it to src/validators/mac_address.py, so no mock replaced the target. Two candidate assertions failed against the real target: test_mixed_separators_are_invalid failed with AssertionError 'mac_address must reject mixed separators: aa:bb-cc-dd:ee:ff ... where False = _rejected(...)', and test_mixed_separators_raise_validation_error_when_requested failed with 'DID NOT RAISE ValidationError'. Both show mac_address returning True (accepted) for the mixed form, exactly the reported actual. The uniform-colon and uniform-hyphen tests passed, confirming the expected true-behavior controls hold. The assertion is on the expected correct behavior (rejection of mixed separators), not an undesired-exception expectation, and the exception handling is limited to ValidationError; failure_refs cite the probe records for these failures. Therefore all three checks hold.

verdicts.reason: The candidate tests assert the contract's expected correct behavior: explicit empty platforms must not be replaced by host platform tags. All three tests executed against the real packaging.tags implementation (target_calls packaging.tags: 149, target source at .../src/packaging/tags.py) and failed exactly as described in the issue. cpython_tags((3,11), abis=["cp311"], platforms=[]) returned host win_amd64 tags instead of []; generic_tags(interpreter="custom", abis=["abi"], platforms=[]) returned host win_amd64 tags instead of []; compatible_tags((3,), interpreter="cp3", platforms=[]) returned host win_amd64 tags plus expected tags instead of the two expected Tag values. The failures therefore match the reported issue and demonstrate the explicit-empty-platforms bug.

The candidate test asserts the exact correct behavior described in the issue: cpython_tags((3,11), abis=["cp311"], platforms=[]) == [], generic_tags(interpreter="custom", abis=["abi"], platforms=[]) == [], and compatible_tags((3,), interpreter="cp3", platforms=[]) == [Tag("cp3","none","any"), Tag("py3","none","any")]. These are regression assertions of the expected outcome, not assertions that expect the buggy exception. The probe confirms the real target module was executed (target_origins maps packaging.tags to the workspace src/packaging/tags.py, 149 target calls, no mocks), and all three tests failed on the call phase with exactly the issue's symptom: explicit empty platforms is treated as omitted, so host platform tags (win_amd64) are substituted. cpython_tags returned 12 items (first extra cp311-cp311-win_amd64), generic_tags returned custom-abi-win_amd64 entries instead of [], and compatible_tags returned py3-none-win_amd64, cp3-none-any, py3-none-any instead of just the two universal tags. Expected assertion, real target execution, and matching failure are all satisfied.
